target.title: fix: skip volatile backup cache paths
target.body:
﻿Fixes #98865

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw backup create` could still traverse disposable agent runtime caches, browser cache/resource-cache trees, retired archive copies, and state-side transient sidecars. Those paths can bloat archives or race with tar even though they have no restoration value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing backup archive path already centralizes volatile filtering through `isVolatileBackupPath`, so this extends that owner boundary instead of adding another archive-time special case. Browser filtering is intentionally scoped to cache-like directories under managed `user-data` paths so durable profile files such as `Preferences` and `Login Data` remain eligible for backup. `.lock` and `.partial` files are scoped to cache, queue, and tmp scratch roots so installed plugin source under `state/extensions` stays backed up.

Issue #98865 was closed manually rather than by a merged runtime fix. I checked current `upstream/main` at `4e6933c84f`, the issue closure events, and related PR search; I found a docs-only open PR (#99007) but no equivalent runtime fix on main.

## User Impact

Backups now skip more disposable runtime/cache files and retired archive copies, reducing archive size and avoiding avoidable live-file races while preserving durable OpenClaw state, browser profile data, and installed plugin source files.

## Evidence

Current head: `2a812d82d93c3e6ef63a15ad3332dfeae0c041c4`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts`  
  Result: passed, 58 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-create.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "surfaces the volatile skip count in the summary"`  
  Result: passed, 1 test, 38 skipped.
- `corepack pnpm docs:list`  
  Result: passed and listed `docs/cli/backup.md`.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.test.ts src/infra/backup-create.ts src/infra/backup-create.test.ts docs/cli/backup.md`  
  Result: passed.
- `git diff --check`  
  Result: passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`  
  Result: exited 0 with no actionable output.

Real archive proof from the changed source path:

- Command: seeded a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then ran `corepack pnpm openclaw backup create --output <temp>/backup-proof.tar.gz --no-include-workspace --json`.
- Result: the CLI completed successfully and returned `"skippedVolatileCount": 8`.
- Archive listing checks after `tar.t(...)`:
  - `OK ABSENT agents/main/agent/cache/provider.json`
  - `OK ABSENT agents/main/agent/shell-snapshots/bash.json`
  - `OK ABSENT cache/shell-snapshots/startup.json`
  - `OK ABSENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Cache/data_0`
  - `OK ABSENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Code Cache/js/index`
  - `OK ABSENT archived/old/openclaw-backup.tar.gz`
  - `OK ABSENT tmp/download.partial`
  - `OK ABSENT tmp/backup.lock`
  - `OK PRESENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Preferences`
  - `OK PRESENT browser/openclaw/user-data/Default/Login Data`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/openclaw.plugin.json`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/bun.lock`
  - `OK PRESENT extensions/demo/download.partial`
  - `OK PRESENT locks/backup.lock`

Not tested: I did not force a live disappearing-file `ENOENT` race during tar traversal; this PR proves the payload boundary with the real `openclaw backup create` path and keeps the existing tar retry behavior covered by the existing tests.
